category_title: Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) showing variable engagement
scenario_title: Social isolation during co-taught individual instruction
minimal_context: The student is working on a math worksheet at their desk while receiving one-on-one instruction from a teacher in a co-taught mainstream classroom.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Here is the math worksheet for today. Let's go through the first few problems together at your desk.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at the worksheet and starts writing the answers, keeping their head down and working alone.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: The students next to you are comparing their answers. You can talk to them.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Continues to look only at the paper, showing no interaction behaviour with the peers nearby.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Why don't you show them what you wrote for number two?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Turns away from the peers to face the teacher completely, continuing to work alone and avoiding any interaction with the rest of the class.)

TUTOR: Here is the math worksheet for today. Let's go through the first few problems together at your desk.

STUDENT: (Turns away from the peers to face the teacher completely, continuing to work alone and avoiding any interaction with the rest of the class.)

task.content: Engaged in core subjects (literacy or maths)

context.social_setting: Co-taught classes with both GET and SET present

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: More frequent implementation of individual teaching to students with SEN by the SET
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Decreased interactions between students with SEN and their peers, and students with ASD work alone more frequently

behavior_patterns.condition: When receiving frequent 1:1 teaching from the SET in a co-taught setting
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Works alone more frequently and interaction with their peers is less frequent
